events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: A Convert for the Gods

options.text: Accept the ways of the pagan gods.
Hold onto your beliefs.
Attempt to convince [character] to convert instead.

events.text: [character] is not timid about sharing his belief that it is wrong for you to follow [religion]. The outspoken pagan claims that [religion] is the true religion of the [rival], the gods tied to our very land and culture. Inviting you to meet in an old pagan temple, [character] offers to teach you the pagan ways. The stony eyes of the statue of watch as you give your answer.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: A Fire Within

options.text: The talk of a divine fight pulls you in...
A true and virtuous life is particularly appealing...
Stay true to your [religion] beliefs.

events.text: [character], a dedicated [religion] believer, has been telling you stories of his god, a divine creator who fights for a perfect world. The tales are captivating and you eagerly ask to hear more. The compelling believer claims that he sees the fire of Ahura Mazda in your eyes and offers to introduce you to a Magi friend of his to learn more of the religion.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: A Poetess in Exile

options.text: Invite [character] to spend her exile living in your court instead.
Let the poetess continue her tour of [family] cities.

events.text: The [family] have been graced by the poetess [character], traveling in exile after her family became embroiled in a violent political scandal. The family bring [character] to perform at the palace, and you listen entranced as she weaves a Hymn to Aphrodite, asking for the goddess’ favor in her pursuit of another woman. The poem is unlike any the court has heard, subtly subverting the structure and language of both epic poems and religious hymns to speak of love. [character] lyrics are already becoming renown, unrivaled whether speaking of the gods or of mortal desires.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: A Quiet Life

options.text: Promise your aid in building these communities.
Incorporate [character] teachings into your own daily life.
Discourage their seclusion from society.

events.text: The austere teachings of [character] have had a profound effect on many of the [religion] clergy, who are gathering in remote communities to reflect on the words of. The are asking for your support in this new practice that they call monasticism.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: A Son of

fields: AddTraitReligion: RELIGION_ZOROASTRIANISM, RELIGION_JUDAISM, RELIGION_CHRISTIANITY, RELIGION_MANICHAEISM, RELIGION_PAGAN_AKSUM, RELIGION_PAGAN_ASSYRIA, RELIGION_PAGAN_BABYLONIA, RELIGION_PAGAN_CARTHAGE, RELIGION_PAGAN_EGYPT, RELIGION_PAGAN_GREECE, RELIGION_PAGAN_KUSH, RELIGION_PAGAN_ROME, RELIGION_PAGAN_PERSIA, RELIGION_PAGAN_HITTITE, RELIGION_ATENISM, RELIGION_HINDUISM, RELIGION_BUDDHISM

options.text: Allow it, [character] will make a fine.
Refuse to hand over your child to the religious leaders.
Refuse to allow it, but hire a religious tutor for [character].

events.text: Your son [character] has taken an increased interest in [religion], spending his days debating theological details with the around the court. Although you pay the discussions little mind, the influence on [character] is not so superficial and he soon comes before you asking to join the ranks of the. Your advisors whisper that. What answer will you give to your ecclesiastically-minded son?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: A Tail of Trouble

options.text: We must be more understanding of [rival] ways.
Leave the priests to simmer, they've already wasted enough time.

events.text: Your Ambassador [character] has just returned from traveling to [rival], where he has been dealing with the fallout of [rival] merchant who inadvertently killed a cat in [city]. The merchant barely escaped a lynching, and was trapped hiding until [character] got him out of the city. Your diligent ambassador has done what he can, but there are still some ruffled feathers among the Egyptian priesthood.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: A World Made Small

options.text: Add your expertise to [character] to plan the building of this grand temple.
Put a call out for engineers and builders to develop the techniques to create this wonder.

tip: As leader: +10% Unit Trait Modifier / Siege
As leader: +10% Unit Trait Modifier / Ship

options.text: Ask [character] about the workings of such constructions.

events.text: You lean in to take a closer look at the figure. Luckily, as an engineer [character] is more skilled at designing buildings, various models of which are scattered around the room. In the center is the one that he brought you here to show. It is a grand structure of stone curving in ways you have never seen. Even this miniature version takes your breath away. [character] says that his vision is for a grand palace to. Will you support the vision?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: A World of Light

options.text: Accept this new interpretation as the standard.
Accept the traditional teachings of the Elect.
Encourage [character] to continue exploring different ideas.

events.text: The cosmology laid down by Mani is a complex tapestry of theologies and divine orders, dictating the order of the universe. Although these systems are a natural inheritor of Gnosticism, [character] has been developing a radical interpretation of the religious books that interprets them as a sign of Revelation with Mani showing the divine will of the heavens.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: ABLANAQANALBA

options.text: Suggest that he starts wearing charms to ward against the magic.
Leave [character] alone.
Offer to inscribe a new sphere.

events.text: [character] shout of frustration echoes down the corridors. Upon entering the room that your scholar has turned into a makeshift workshop, a crystal sphere slams into the wall a hair-breadth from your royal head. "My [title]!" he exclaims, "I did not think anyone else was here!" After profuse apologies, [character] explains that he was trying to inscribe a crystal globe with the old word of power ABLANAQANALBA, a palindrome spell. Picking up and inspecting the ball makes it clear what is wrong, the word has an extra letter, spelled wrong just before completion. [character] seems convinced that the mistake has brought some kind of curse upon him.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Abandoned by

options.text: Encourage [character] to at least make a show of following [religion].
Exile [character] for his impiety.

tip: As leader: -40 Opinion with all Religions

options.text: Refuse to condemn [character] for his ideas.

events.text: [character] stands accused of impiety and of being a 'godless person', by extension undermining the authority of [rival]. The court are pushing to impeach the <p.is_sub.S0=SUBJECT_HAS_JOB>[title]<else>courtier<end> to stymie his immoral influence.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Against the Unholy

options.text: Warn [character] of the danger.
Let the plan go ahead.
Convince [character] and [character] to rethink their actions.

events.text: [character] and [character] may often disagree when it comes to faith, but against [character] they stand united. The unlikely friends are often found discussing the unwanted influence of the mage in court, putting the differences of [religion] and [religion] aside to imagine what devious practices he may be up to next. You have become aware of a plot brewing, planning for [character] to be attacked by 'bandits' on the way home one evening. Will you intercede to protect the mage?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Alexander, or the False Prophet

options.text: Allow the opening of a cult shrine to Glycon in [city].
Ask Alexander and Glycon for a gift with blessings of fertility.
What an obvious sham! Have this false prophet arrested.

events.text: [character] has become embroiled in a conflict with a growing cult in [city], run by a Greek prophet Alexander. [character] says that the 'false prophet' carries around a snake with a head of golden hair, which he claims is the god Glycon - an incarnation of Asclepius. While [character] makes every effort to show that this sacred snake is but a hand puppet in a wig, the popularity of the cult continues to grow. You are informed that there has even been a petition to build a cult shrine in [city] as a center of healing and fertility.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: All But a Name

options.text: Have your scribes compose a treatise on the differences between your gods.

tip: As leader: +5% State Religion Spread Chance

options.text: We do not need to take action, is clearly beyond compare.

requirements.label: Inquisitive
tip: The leader must have Inquisitive (a character trait)

options.text: Research the cultural links between your pantheons.

events.text: There have been a number of texts comparing the gods of your pantheon to those of [rival], saying the two are alike in all but their names. The court are outraged. Your gods are clearly superior to those of [rival]!

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Amulets and Charms

options.text: Gladly take the amulet!
Refuse such superstitions.

events.text: [character] has crafted an amulet which he claims is imbued with protection. "You may be able to afford the best doctors and healers, but the help of the gods is always valuable."

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Bema

options.text: We are cleansed!
Strive to control yourself better in the year ahead.

events.text: No matter how closely you strive to follow the commandments of [religion], it is impossible to lead a completely holy life. This is what it is to be human. To atone for these failings, both the Elect and Hearers go through ritual purification and confession weekly. The culmination of this atonement is during the Bema festival, four days marking the end of a month of fasting. As people gather together around Mani's throne in confession through hymns and the rites of eating, they are forgiven for the sins of the past year.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Beneath the Surface

options.text: Make sacrifices to appease the gods.
Send soldiers to guard the ships.
The people of [city] can look after themselves.

events.text: Merchants and fishermen trade tales like no one else. The latest stories are not a consoling tale. The rumor has spread that the seas around [city] are being thrown into chaos by or some other vengeful god. The elders of the city say that the rumors are starting to disrupt their trade and beg for you to intervene.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Brother against Brother

options.text: Have [character] speak with [character] on your behalf.

requirements.label: Charming character / Covert
tip: The leader must have one of: Charming character (a character trait); Covert (a character trait)

options.text: Lead the meeting with [character], with [character] support.
Refuse the help and lure the most fervent rebels into a fight.

events.text: The threat of civil war hangs over [rival]. The divide between the [family], fierce supporters of your rule, and the [family], who are opposed to you, grows deeper every day. The smallest conflict could break out into full-blown war. Aware of the ruin that such conflict could bring, [character] offers to intervene to help to placate the discontent [family].

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Building Favor

options.text: Take the bribe to deny the construction.

events.text: [character] is an adherent follower of [religion], driven by his <p.is_sub.S2=SUBJECT_PIOUS>pious<p=SUBJECT_ZEALOT>zealous<else>devout<end> nature. He has petitioned the court for permission to construct a new Temple to in the capital, dedicated in the [family] name. [character] has asked that you reject the proposal, as it will overshadow a small shrine previously constructed by the [family]. The [title] is prepared to pay for your support. Will you allow the construction to go ahead?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Called to Mission

options.text: Fund the's evangelical mission.
Refuse, [character] is needed in court.

events.text: [character] has been called by, when that showed him making a journey across distant lands to bring [religion] to new followers. [character] believes that it is his calling to travel to [rival] and asks for your patronage. Will you fund this journey?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Carmen

options.text: Hire a retainer to teach [character] the art of verse.
Demand that [character] stops his chanting.

events.text: [character] is in the habit of composing small chants in verse that he often repeats to himself. The words you catch include the names of the various gods of [religion] and mythological figures. It is little surprise that some in the court are fearful that the young ward is cursing them. [character] suggests encouraging this predilection for verse, although warns that the line between lyrics and spells is a fine one indeed. Although most would use a seer if needed, the support of such practices and practitioners changes as often as the tide.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Charged with Corruption

options.text: [character] is to be deposed, stripped of all titles and sent to exile.
[character] is right, he deserves a fair trial.

requirements.label: Corrupt / Schemer
tip: The leader must have one of: Corrupt; Schemer

options.text: Pay bribes for the charges to be dropped and stability restored.

events.text: You have been asked to preside over the [religion] High Synod, at which the religious head [character] is to defend himself against charges of corruption. A group of led by [character], claim that [character] commanded soldiers to burn their homes after falsely claiming that they were dissidents. Brought forth to apologize, [character] refuses to recognize the legality of a Synod in which his open enemies are sitting as judges. Your advisors suggest that this could be a chance to rid yourself of the upset [title], although the leader remains popular with many of the [rival] populace.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Child of the River

options.text: Encourage the claims.
Encourage [character] to follow a life of piety.
Be glad of the family you have!

events.text: [character] supporters, ever looking to shower praise upon their leader, have started claiming that he is the child of a river nymph. Although at first embarrassed, [character] seems to enjoy the idea and now tells the story himself.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Christian Asceticism

options.text: Encourage this journey of self-improvement.

fields: AddTraitReligion: RELIGION_ZOROASTRIANISM, RELIGION_JUDAISM, RELIGION_CHRISTIANITY, RELIGION_MANICHAEISM, RELIGION_PAGAN_AKSUM, RELIGION_PAGAN_ASSYRIA, RELIGION_PAGAN_BABYLONIA, RELIGION_PAGAN_CARTHAGE, RELIGION_PAGAN_EGYPT, RELIGION_PAGAN_GREECE, RELIGION_PAGAN_KUSH, RELIGION_PAGAN_ROME, RELIGION_PAGAN_PERSIA, RELIGION_PAGAN_HITTITE, RELIGION_ATENISM, RELIGION_HINDUISM, RELIGION_BUDDHISM

options.text: Maybe [character] has found a calling in the clergy.
Ask [character] to speak well of you in his letters.

events.text: What is the relation between the body and spirit? Some things that [rival] have taken for granted are now being challenged by the [religion] religion. A lack of material goods and denying the body food can now be seen as a moral and noble path. [character] has been seeking self improvement and writing to [character] for guidance. Your child wants to dedicate himself to. What will you suggest?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Claims of Divergence

options.text: Charge [character] with crimes of divergence.
Let [character] go with a warning.

events.text: For too long has [character] been a threat to your rule. There is a rare opportunity to be done with this thorn once and for all. A regular contact of [character] has been exposed as a follower of a divergent branch of [religion] belief. Outspoken and potentially dangerous, the Orthodoxy laws of [rival] mean that this crime is punishable by death. It would be easy to accuse [character] of the same crime, using their friendship as evidence. Will you use this extreme measure?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Collegia

options.text: Abandon the Collegia system for a priestly caste.
Tell the priests to get in line, lest they bring the anger of the gods on [rival].
[character] should learn to relax!

events.text: [character] has a problem. Rather than a priestly caste, the positions of [religion] are filled by well-off citizens elected to colleges. Although centered around religion, these colleges are an important social point, allowing the members to foster friendships and engage in social activities. This year's members, [character] complains, are focusing rather too much on carousing and relinquishing their religious duties.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Come to Collect

options.text: Lament your role in this tragedy.
It must be a trick of the light.
Throw yourself at the feet of.

events.text: Dark visions haunt you and strange creatures lurk in the corner of your sight. Surely <p.is_sub.S1=SUBJECT_ZOROASTRIANISM>this is Araska, the Daeva of vengeance<p=SUBJECT_CHRISTIANITY>these are the servants of the Devil<p=SUBJECT_RELIGION_GREECE>these are the furies of Hades<else>this is some god of vengeance<end>, sent to chase you to your end?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Communion

options.text: Instruct that a temple of worship be built.
Agree that the [religion] cannot be trusted.

events.text: The [religion] of [city] have been struggling to find space to hold their communions, gatherings where the faithful break bread in the memory of their god. The [family] are reluctant to give more ground to the religion, worried that people gathering in such large numbers will be a breeding ground for public unrest.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Contemplation through Music

options.text: Have them focus on their own cities.
Poetry should be studied by all.

events.text: Some of [character] followers seem confused by their teacher’s fascination with music and poetry. The esteemed philosopher replies with a speech before the court, compellingly pursuing the idea that art is a vital part of a thriving society, encouraging a good understanding of ethics, emotion and the natural order of heaven and earth. The [family] are particularly taken with the idea and propose to build the study of poetry into the teachings of all [rival] children.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Contender

options.text: Accept the demands.
Force [character] into the clergy.

events.text: The angry [character] has found a powerful ally in [religion]. The upset followers of the religion have thrown their lot in with the successor who has made promises that they will be well treated if he takes the throne. [character] has enough support that he boldly declares an ultimatum: Rework the succession to make him the heir or he will stir discontent among the [religion].

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Cursed

options.text: All is lost!

tip: As leader: -40 Opinion with all Religions

options.text: Ignore the ‘curse’.

events.text: News has reached you that [character], driven by his anger and hatred for you, has cursed your name and performed sacrifices asking for to strike you down.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Death, God and Taxes

outcomes.label: Death God And Taxes Option 0 State
Death God And Taxes Option 0 Clerks

options.text: Refuse, [religion] will be treated the same as all others.

events.text: Inspired by the religion's within [rival], the [religion] leader [character] has come before you to a favor. The noble [title] asks that the [religion] temples are given a tax exemption, to better serve. A grant like this will certainly make friends with the, but are you willing to make an exception?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Deep Divisions

requirements.label: Religious / Diplomat
tip: The leader must have one of: Religious (a character trait); Diplomat

options.text: Convince the leaders to work together.

events.text: [character] has come to you, warning of a dangerous divide splitting the [religion] community. The of [city] are championing the ideals of [theology], while the of [city] support the doctrine of [theology]. [character] has been unable to bridge the divide and looks to you for support.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Descended From Astarte

options.text: Give [character] control of the nation's education.
Appoint him to a role as special advisor.
Refuse to grant any more powers to the [title].

events.text: The legends of [rival] say that Queen Dido brought the High Priest of Astarte across the seas with her, promising him and his descendants the position of High Priest in her new city. [character], the current head of [religion], claims that the rights of the role have dwindled across the years and is looking to restore the position to power.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Dining with Divinity

options.text: Their home will be a temple, with [character] as the.
Invite them to bring their story to the priests of [city].

tip: As leader: -40 Opinion with all Religions

options.text: Have the land resettled, it is nothing but superstition.

events.text: There are tales in [city] of an elderly couple who claim to have entertained at dinner after the rest of the town turned the disguised god away. The town was then hit by a flood, in which the two farmers were the only ones to survive. They request that their old house be rededicated as a temple to the gods.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Discovered by

options.text: Invite them to share their knowledge with the court.
This is a task for our scouts, not the priests.

events.text: The of [religion] have made contact with a distant nation on their travels. They eagerly seek a meeting to discuss the people they call [rival].

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Divine Inspiration

options.text: Adapt the story into a dramatic poem.
Carve a sculpture of the dramatic scene.
Compose a masterful piece on how the lessons of the story still echo today.
Write a treatise on the historical figures involved in the story.

events.text: You have heard the philosophers speak of how inspiration is a gift from but you paid such thoughts little mind. The words return to you however; after hearing a particularly beautiful verse adapting a story from the you are moved to compose your own work in praise of the divine. The [family], who commissioned the artist who so inspired you, praise your exclamation and ask to see the work as soon as it is completed.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Easter

options.text: Convene a Synod to decide on a date.
Remind [character] on the importance of forgiveness.
Leave the matter to the clergy.

events.text: Since Christ's first disciples, it has been a tradition to celebrate the day that Jesus rose again from the tomb, gradually replacing the Judaism festival of Passover amongst the [religion]. What is less certain is the date that should be celebrated. Despite varying opinions, it has never been a serious debate until now. [character] has expelled a of [city] for saying that the day occurs part way through the month. The other ask you to intercede with the [religion] leader.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Ecstatic Cult

options.text: Allow the cult to take root.
Forbid ecstatic worship without the permission of the state.

events.text: The people of [city] have had little exposure to the rites of [religion] until now. This makes it all the more shocking when the cult of <p.is_sub.S0=SUBJECT_PLAYER_GREECE>Dionysus<p=SUBJECT_PLAYER_ROME>Bacchus<else>a recently adapted foreign god<end> takes hold in the city. This god of revelry and his mystery cult soon have a loyal following of initiates. Reports say that the initiates leave the city at night and roam the lands around the city, casting off their clothes and losing themselves in wild dancing and celebration. The other citizens of [city] are worried about the immorality this cult might bring to the city.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Family Ghosts

options.text: Call upon [character] for protection.
Ask for [character] guidance.
Refuse the help of such superstitions.

events.text: It has become common practice for the people of [rival] to construct household shrines to honor the ghosts of their ancestors. Simple structures, these conduits are tucked in the corner of the room for sacrifice and prayers. Even in death, the ancestors of the living protect the family and the home. Coming from a noble line you have kings and queens to call on. To whom will you pray?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Feeding the Gods

options.text: Gift the temples grain from [rival]'s stockpiles.
Promise to build up the nation's supplies.
Such a situation is a risk worth taking.

events.text: Every day, the statues of the gods of [rival] are washed and clothed by priests. Their feet are bathed and anointed with perfume as food and beer is laid out as an offering. [character] makes a request to build a stockpile of food in the temples for such offerings, in case of harvests or famine. Without offerings, the gods might abandon the city, leading to disaster and ruin.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Festival of the Fravashi

options.text: Offer veneration to the warlike aspects of the departed.
Give focus to the stories of rebirth and protection.
Pay honor to your family ancestors.

events.text: In the final days of each year, festivals are held to invoke the help of the Fravashi. These beings are a host of warrior spirits of the dead who fought alongside Ahura Mazda, made up of the pious and righteous ancestors of the living. As you prepare the meals and offerings for the spirits, your mind turns to what aid you will ask for.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Final Inheritance

options.text: Yes, use this chance to amend your inheritance.
No, [character] must take the throne.

events.text: As you lie unmoving on your bed your unhappy heir [character] stands to one side, completely uninterested in the litany of prayers, hopes for health and premature mourning taking place around you. [character] leans in to whisper so that only you may hear, "he followers of [religion] trust in you enough that if you wished to amend the issue of your succession, the stand ready to ensure that all believe that your chosen heir is also the chosen of." Such actions will anger [character], but it is rare to get such a chance without people questioning the legitimacy of your dynasty. Will [character] remain the heir?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Flight from the Body

options.text: We should embrace these teachings and see where they guide us.
I too will strive for separation from the body.
There is so much to be learned from these ideas!

events.text: [character] has spent the week on the steps of the palace, speaking on the nature of ethics and the Neoplatonist desire of emulating the incorporeal divine. This contemplation of God and the emphasis on a spiritual world apart from the material has had a profound effect on the [religion] followers in [city].

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Four Elements

options.text: Mithra, of the covenants and rising sun.
Atar, the god of fire.
Anahita, of health, water and wisdom.
Refuse to make a sacrifice.

events.text: The rituals of [religion] start with fire, created on an altar, and pass through the elements to water, a bringer of life. [character] has prepared a ritual for the new year, gathering the required elements and offerings for the sacrifices. Which god will receive your sacrifice?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Fragments of her Voice

options.text: Leave [character] to her thoughts.
Determine to take the scribes to task over this loss.

events.text: You are shocked to hear that a vast collection of [character] earlier poems have been destroyed under the careless mismanagement of your scribes. However, when presented with the burned remains the poet seems unaffected by the loss, instead marveling at the beauty in the fragments. “Each alone, adrift. But drawn to each other.” She speaks, to no one but herself.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Gayomartan

options.text: Order regular sacrifices to the elements and the gods of order.
Strive to follow Ahura Mazda's order in your daily life.

events.text: The legends of [religion] tell of how Ahura Mazda created the first man, Gayomartan, from the death of the first bull whose corpse gave birth to all animals. Gayomartan was so beautiful that Angra Mainyu killed him and it is from his death that mortal humans were born. But these mortals were deceived by Angra Mainyu's whispered lies and they fell from grace. It is up to the rest of humanity to give support to Ahura Mazda against the disorder of Angra Mainyu. How will you give your support?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: General Devotion

options.text: Promote one of the officers to replace [character] as General.
Bring [character] back in line with a reminder of a General’s duties.
Suggest that [character] inducts the officers into the cult to form camaraderie in the ranks.

events.text: The General [character] has become infatuated with the <p.is_sub.S0=SUBJECT_CITY_CULT_HEALER>Cult Of The Healer<p=SUBJECT_CITY_CULT_MITHRAS>Cult Of Mithras<p=SUBJECT_CITY_CULT_ISIS>Cult Of Isis And Serapis<p=SUBJECT_CITY_CULT_MOTHER>Cult Of The Mother<p=SUBJECT_CITY_CULT_ECSTATIC>Ecstatic Cult<p=SUBJECT_CITY_CULT_ANGELIC_DIVINE>Cult Of The Angelic Divine<p=SUBJECT_CITY_CULT_DUAL>Dual Cult<p=SUBJECT_CITY_CULT_MARTYR>Martyr Cult<p=SUBJECT_CITY_CULT_AMAZON>Amazon Cult<p=SUBJECT_CITY_CULT_CAVALRY>Cavalry Cult<p=SUBJECT_CITY_CULT_FALLEN>Shrine Of The Fallen Goddess<p=SUBJECT_CITY_CULT_HERO>Shrine Of The Hero<p=SUBJECT_CITY_CULT_SWORD>Sword Cult<p=SUBJECT_CITY_CULT_CONSORT>Gods Consort Shrine<else>local cult<end> in [city], spending much of his time participating in rituals for the cult and delegating command to his officers. The ungoverned soldiers are becoming unruly and impatient, spending their time drinking and seeking out brawls in the camp. Seeking help, the officers have come to you to ask for order to be restored.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Heads of Faith

options.text: Encourage the leaders to resolve their problems in a public debate.
Demand that they keep civil within the boundaries of your court.
Invite the two to share a meal with you to resolve their problems.

events.text: Managing one religion is quite a task, but your nation has the heads of two residing within your court. The [religion] [character] and [religion] [character] unsurprisingly refuse to see eye-to-eye, with the deep animosity growing as each tries to further their religion's role within [rival]. The tension has reached a head with the two normally dignified leaders having a shouting match in front of the court and visiting dignitaries. You need to bring these heads of faith in line, but how?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Holy Days

options.text: Take as many as needed!
Maybe this has gotten a little out of hand…

events.text: The holy days of [religion] are a cause of celebration and reflection, with people lining the streets across [rival]. Your council are worried about the steadily increasing number of holy days, with a new one added for every victory and holy birthday.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Holy Teachers

options.text: Accept these radical ideas as a part of [religion].
Refuse to entertain these ideas.

events.text: Ever seeking to learn more of the divine, [character] regularly seeks out those with a reputation of being holy teachers. He claims that seeking out these different views tests his faith and leads to a deepened understanding of. Returning from the latest trip, [character] is almost fervent with ideas of [theology] and how they reframe the.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Homer and Hesiod

options.text: Attempt to have the texts written down in.
Sponsor new poets to learn and retell the story.
Retell the stories through a wide-ranging program of sculpture.
Let the stories fend for themselves.

events.text: The stories of the gods of [rival] have been handed down generation to generation. These tales from the near-mythical poets Homer and Hesiod tell of the forging of the world, the fates in the stars, the schemes of the gods and the hubris of man. Such a tradition is a vital part of the nation's culture, although some are worried that such tales will soon be lost without aid.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Humility of the Wise

options.text: Welcome [character] to your court.
Refuse the [tribe] traveler.

events.text: You are approached by a [tribe] traveler, [character], a prince of his people renowned for journeying to different lands to gain wisdom. Bowing before you, the noble speaks, "I have traveled here from afar to make you my friend. Allow me into your court and I will stay for a few years before returning to my people." Will you accept this visitor from another land?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Illegal Shrine

options.text: Assign administrators to organize and oversee the construction of such sites.
Allow the construction of shrines without a licence.
Banish all cult worship that has not been approved by your court.

events.text: The number of sanctioned cults in [rival] has encouraged the devotees of lesser known gods to build shrines to their deities whenever and wherever they can. [character] comes before you, complaining that a cult shrine has been built right in the center of the [family] family seat of [city] without permission. The [family] demand that limits be placed on the building of shrines, a practice that the [religion] resist.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Illuminated Text

options.text: Donate the gift to the.
Display the text in your court.
Sell the book on to a collector of rare texts.

events.text: Encouraged to have such strong allies in the faith, [character] has sent the lavish gift of a tome of [religion] teachings bound in gold and jewels. The parchment is carefully illustrated with paintings of mythical creatures and religious figures. The court gasps upon seeing such beauty, some offering prayers to.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Immoral Mysteries

options.text: Command [character] to stop partaking in the rituals.
Allow the meetings to continue.

events.text: On a recent visit to [city], your son [character] was initiated into the Mysteries of the <p.is_sub.S0=SUBJECT_CITY_CULT_MITHRAS>Cult Of Mithras<p=SUBJECT_CITY_CULT_ISIS>Cult Of Isis And Serapis<p=SUBJECT_CITY_CULT_MOTHER>Cult Of The Mother<p=SUBJECT_CITY_CULT_ECSTATIC>Ecstatic Cult<p=SUBJECT_CITY_CULT_DUAL>Dual Cult<p=SUBJECT_CITY_CULT_AMAZON>Amazon Cult<p=SUBJECT_CITY_CULT_CAVALRY>Cavalry Cult<p=SUBJECT_CITY_CULT_SWORD>Sword Cult<else>local cult<end>. Some of [character] fellow initiates have returned to the capital with the young prince and the group are regularly gathering in the palace for nights of drunken revelry. [character] insists that this is all part of the cult worship, but many in the court are concerned that the prince may be twisting the rites for his own enjoyment.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: In All Things

options.text: Speak out about the moral corruption of studying such occult lore.
This power is nothing to be feared.

events.text: There is no such thing as magic. Or at least no one such thing as magic. The people of [rival] use small superstitions every day as they go about their lives. But the same people who use these services are the first to turn against the person they don't understand. [character] has been leading the charge against practitioners like [character], claiming that the idea of magic wields far too much power among the masses.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Isis and Serapis

options.text: Welcome the worship of Isis and Serapis.
Allow the cult, but create laws to limit their influence.
Refuse entry to these foreign gods.

events.text: The port-city of [city] sees a steady flow of travelers entering by sea, merchants and diplomats from distant lands risking the perilous seas. The latest residents are unlike all others. The gods Isis and Serapis have been brought by visitors from [rival] and have gained enough of a following in the city that there are calls to build a shrine for the cult. Your advisors warn that they've heard that the cult is being spread in a deliberate plan by [character] to gain influence in other lands. Will you permit this worship?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Joined in Mystery

options.text: Do what you can for your fellow initiate.
My role as [title] must take priority above all, even the mysteries.

events.text: Being a part of a cult joins you to people from all walks of [rival] life. Often a blessing, it can also prove a curse. [character] has accused a lesser noble of theft, and this unsavory character, almost certainly guilty, has called upon you for a pardon as a fellow member of the mysteries.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Led by the Stars

options.text: Expel all divination from the city.
Forbid readings in private or on the matter of deaths.
Seek out their advice yourself.

events.text: [character] is worried about the future after a recent trip to [city]. The portents of astrology are so widely believed there that people pay more attention to diviners than to official edicts. The courtier suggests expelling astrology from the city before it becomes even more powerful.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Letters of Faith

options.text: Allow the growth of a [religion] community in [city].
Demand that [character] stops sending these letters.

events.text: There is a steadily growing community of [religion] faithful in [city], encouraged by their close correspondence with the believer [character]. The encouragement of this budding faith has drawn the ire of the [family]. The family are less than happy with a different faith to their own taking hold in their cities and ask you to intervene.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Listening to the Tanakh

options.text: Ask to hear more from [character].
Engage in a vigorous debate.
Ask [character] to keep it down.

events.text: Every week, on the day known as the sabbath, [character] joins the other [religion] faithful in listening to a reading of passages from the. As you pass by, an especially interesting phrase catches your attention. Before long passing by and listening in to the readings is a regular part of your week. [character] notices and asks if you want to learn more about [religion].

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Lucky in Love

options.text: Oh to find a love blessed even by the gods!
[character] is so talented with his words, ask to learn this skill.
Profess your admiration for [character].

events.text: [character] voice is enchanting, the rhythmic speech weaving a tale of two long separated lovers, reunited when begs to move the stars to allow the two to be united.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Miracle Worker

options.text: Claim that's power is undeniable and should be supported throughout [rival].
Agree that [character] is surely blessed.
Retort that you are yet to see any miracles.

events.text: The gathered crowd fall into a reverent hush as [character] steps into the hall. There have been rumors of the [title] performing miracles through the power of such as levitation and changing elements. Although [character] refuses to perform such acts on demand, [character] is utterly convinced and promises to follow [religion]. He turns to you, "Are [character] acts not a sign of's unending power?"

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Miracle Worker

options.text: Claim that's power is undeniable and should be supported throughout [rival].
Agree that [character] is surely blessed.
Retort that you are yet to see any miracles.

events.text: The gathered crowd fall into a reverent hush as [character] steps into the hall. There have been rumors of the [title] performing miracles through the power of such as levitation and changing elements. Although [character] refuses to perform such acts on demand, [character] is utterly convinced and promises to follow [religion]. He turns to you, "Are [character] acts not a sign of's unending power?"

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Mocking the Mysteries

options.text: Charge the poet with destroying a statue, but not impiety.
Agree that such impiety must be met with exile.

tip: As leader: -40 Opinion with all Religions

options.text: Maybe there is some wisdom to his arguments...

events.text: The people of [city] have asked for you to pass judgment on a poet who has been terrorizing the city. First chopping up a wooden statue of to cook on, the poet [character] has also been openly revealing the mysteries of the local cults. [character] is completely unrepentant, denying the very existence of the gods.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: More than Stories

options.text: The new readings of the tales inspire you to start writing your own.
[character] should not be permitted to influence the public like that.
Praise [character] for his defense of the classics against new schools of thought.

events.text: Ever the orator, [character] has taken to the streets with an impassioned speech on hidden meanings lying within the tales of [religion]. Although the allegorical reading certainly refutes the claims that the earlier poets were impious, some claim that these readings are simply hiding [character] own beliefs.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: My Brother in

options.text: Spare no expense in convincing [character] of your good intentions.
Attempt to win him over with your natural charm.
Refuse to make concessions for the [religion] leader.

events.text: It is common to get regular correspondence from important figures in your court, including the [title] of your state religion, [character]. Unlike the courtesy due your position and rank, [character] messages are often terse and openly criticize your approach to leadership. Your agents close to the [title] say that as a <p.is_sub.S2=SUBJECT_TACTICIAN>Commander Archetype, [character] loathes your study of tactics rather than commanding from the front lines.<p=SUBJECT_JUDGE>Schemer Archetype, [character] loathes your strict observance for the rules and the insistence that others live up to such standards.<p=SUBJECT_ORATOR>Diplomat Archetype, [character] claims that you could bring people together but instead use the ability to twist words for your own gain.<p=SUBJECT_SCHOLAR>Zealot Archetype, [character] loathes your preference to reading and studying rather than taking action.<p=SUBJECT_BUILDER>Hero Archetype, [character] loathes your preference for planning cities and buildings rather than riding to battle.<p=SUBJECT_SCHEMER>Judge Archetype, [character] loathes your apparent disregard for following the same rules as everyone else.<p=SUBJECT_COMMANDER>Tactician Archetype, [character] claims that you lack tactical thought, both on the field of battle and off of it.<p=SUBJECT_HERO>Builder Archetype, [character] loathes your love for fast action and heroics rather than slowly building up your cities.<p=SUBJECT_ZEALOT>Scholar Archetype, [character] claims that you are too willing to fight for a cause with little thought for the consequences.<p=SUBJECT_DIPLOMAT>Orator Archetype, [character] envies your ability to easily make friends, even without as much skill with words.<else>leader of opposite character, [character] struggles to relate to you.<end> Will you try to heal this divide?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Naos

options.text: Make a donation to the city shrine.
Assign more priests as caretakers for the shrine.
Argue that such donations are the responsibility of the [family].

events.text: Where do the gods reside? Popular [rival] thought is that their shrines and temples are inhabited by the gods, or at least visited during their rituals. However, the actual rites require open space outside with a raised altar for sacrifices and libations. These sacred sites depend on financial donations to survive and the priests of [city] have come asking for such a donation, saying that the shrine is falling into disrepair.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: National Unity

options.text: Lead a persecution of [religion].
Try to win over the [religion] leaders instead.
Refuse to continue to support [religion] after the suggestion.

events.text: The institute that is [religion] is increasingly important in your nation, but it is not the only religion. Although the various faiths within [rival] can normally co-exist with only the occasional argument, [character] makes the case that the spread of [religion] is a danger to national unity given their less-than-favorable view of your rule. He suggests a firm hand will be the best course for national unity.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Offerings to Tyre

options.text: Refuse to pay more dues.
Encourage the city to pay, to avoid displeasing the gods.
Persuade the priests to settle in [rival].

events.text: The Temple of Melqart in Tyre still demands donations from the cities of [religion]. The priestly class of Phoenicia claim the Carthaginian gods as their own, but the gods of the pantheon, although many sailed across the seas with your people, are born from a mix of the traditional and local gods of the land you now call [rival]. The people of [city] have been called on to pay their dues. Will you uphold this tradition?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: One Above All

options.text: Agree that should be given honors above the other gods.

tip: As leader: +5% State Religion Spread Chance

options.text: Demand that the priests include all of the gods in their rites.

events.text: Your association with has set both of you apart. You are granted legitimacy beyond all people and is marked as above the other gods. Perhaps because of this influence, the priests of [religion] have been making increasingly drastic changes to the rites of the religion, elevating alone. Some of the court are worried that this will bring the wrath of the jilted gods.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Open DISSENT
events.text: You, along with the rest of [city], have been made aware of [character] radical ideas after he took to the steps of the palace to give a speech on the "true" meaning of the. After the sermon, [character] reveals that he has joined a small radical sect of [religion]. Your advisors warn that the sect has some rather extreme beliefs about the use of violence to bring about the will of.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Other World

options.text: Learn the art of their bards.
Learn the wisdom of their druids.
Spend your time teaching [character] about [religion].
Turn the [tribe] delegation away.

events.text: [character] has arrived at your court with a cohort of [tribe] vates, bards and druids. Your court are wary of the influence of these strange people but there could be much to learn from their ways and tales of the 'other world'.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Our Pantheon Spreads

options.text: Organize a long-term deal with official trade routes.
Agree to sell the city official amulets.
Place a strict embargo to stop the trade.

events.text: The [rival] have many gods of their own, but a recent trend in [city] has seen the amulets and icons of your own [religion] gaining in popularity. Although the markets of the city are already filled with [rival] amulets, and [rival] replicas, [character] has sent an envoy to try and organize a steady supply of the now-valuable items.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Poet in Vogue

options.text: Bring the poet to court to have your fortune divined.
Let the court have their fun, but state your scepticisms about such signs.
Exile the poet to rid the court of his influence.

events.text: The court has been gripped by the words of an astrological poet, whose horoscopes and handbooks are quickly becoming the go-to source for divining the movements of the stars and planets. The popularity of this poet is steadily growing. Will you engage with such divination?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Religious Truce

options.text: Agree to honor the truce.
Refuse to listen to the diplomats' pleas.

events.text: Diplomats from [rival] have arrived with an unusual request. They are approaching a significant [religion] festival and are requesting a temporary truce to be able to focus on their religious observances.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Respect for the Gods

options.text: Make extra donations to the shrine to show your dedication.
Promise to respect all of the gods equally.
Refuse to listen to the family's complaints.

events.text: The [family] are outraged that there is a competing god in [rival], claiming that you have been showing favor to the shrine of [city] over that of [city]. The family warn that their deity has been successfully protecting the nation and that raising the status of other gods is a great disrespect. How will you reply to this claim of disrespect?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Rumors of Ostanes

options.text: Send people to [rival] to search for Ostanes.
Ban any texts by Ostanes.
Threaten to burn all magical texts, and any who follow them.

events.text: It is rumored that in the court of [rival] there is a [religion] capable of harnessing the elements and speaking with the dead. These practices of 'magic' are unusual for even the magi. Perhaps for this reason, although many alchemical treatises have been attributed to this practitioner, no one seems to have met the fabled Ostanes. Now a new treatise bearing his name is being passed around by members of the court, an account of the practices of magic which is gripping the imagination of your subjects.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Sacred Chastity

tip: As leader: -40 Opinion with all Religions

options.text: Your duty is to this family before!
Do what you must.

events.text: Inspired by his [religion] faith, [character] has reached the idea that it is vital that he stays chaste for. Although not a common part of the religion, the idea of sacred chastity has started to spread as a part of the religion's dialog with morality.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Sacred Scripture

options.text: Advise that it is better not to upset the faction.
Send your armies to detain the rebellious clergy.

events.text: What words are sacred? [character] has been dealing with this very problem, as the of [religion] argue over which passages and texts belong as a part of the. One passage carries an implication of [theology], which although the wider clergy agree it should be removed, the of [city] are fighting to have it included. The weary [character] asks if you would advise conceding to these determined clerics.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Sayer and Speaker

options.text: We have made our choice. Now we fight.

events.text: No sooner have you issued your decree than reports arrive of an invasion aimed at [city]. Was it the word of the gods or a lucky guess?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Seeking Repentance

options.text: Publicly beg [character] for forgiveness.
Refuse to act in such a humiliating manner.

events.text: Relations with [character] are strained, the aloof [title] making his distaste clear in every meeting and every message. Although [character] seems to have judged you lacking in the standards he expects in a [title] supporting [religion], he believes in [theology]. This idea of freeing people from bondage has expanded into a sense that it is right to forgive the genuinely repentant. A dramatic enough gesture could earn the forgiveness of [character] and, but are you willing to throw yourself at the feet of another?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Seeking Solitude

options.text: Approve his retirement.
No, there is still much to be done.

events.text: [character] has been distracted of late, his attention often drifting away during meetings. Finally the elderly courtier comes to you with a request, to retire to the Monastery of [city] to live out the rest of his days in the presence of. Will you relinquish your courtier?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Seizing the Mantle

options.text: Support [character] as the new leader of [religion].
Imprison [character] for inciting violence.
Send your army to expel any [religion] involved in the fighting.

events.text: Transitions of power are rarely seamless, and sadly the same is true for the [religion]. In a vicious bid for the title of [title], [character] has been leading bloody riots through the streets of [city]. The chaos threatens to spill across the nation unless something is done swiftly. [character]. How will you intercept this attempt to displace the [title] from power?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Sins of Ingratitude

options.text: Count your blessings and strive for a light heart.
[character] is right, these rituals are not for a [title].

events.text: To pass the judgment of Osiris in the afterlife, a person's soul must be as light as one of Ma'at's feathers. Such harmony is easy to lose track of, but a new practice has arisen, called the Five Gifts of Hathor. People use the fingers of their hand to count five specific things that they are grateful for. Without gratitude, it is thought that dark energy will cloud a person's soul and lead them down a path of sin. When you are encouraged to try it by the court, [character] argues that such humility is not seemly for a [title] such as yourself.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Son of the Star

options.text: Make an agreement for [character] to lead the city as a semi-autonomous state.
Send forces to fight [character] for the city.
Use scorched-earth tactics to run him to ground.

events.text: As the Dissent Judaism has taken hold in [city], a leader has risen who has united the [religion] against your local forces. [character] has a reputation as a harsh but effective leader, punishing any who refuse to join his ranks. Swift action will needed to be taken if we are to keep [city] from falling into [character] control.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Statue of

options.text: Pay the costs for construction to begin.
Refuse to back this folly.

events.text: The laws of [rival] protect the worship of gods through images and icons, and the priests of [religion] have devised plans for the grandest statue of all. Together with the [family] family they have designed a grand temple structure to stand in the Holy City of [city]. Within the temple will rest a towering statue of, seated in true majesty. The [family] alone cannot fund such a colossal undertaking and seek your sponsorship. A temple of such scale is no small project, and your architects estimate that it will take ten years to be built. Will you pay for such a grand project?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Strike Them Down

options.text: Agree to stop the [religion] menace.
Refuse to help the zealous clergy.
[character] wields too much power. Exile him.

events.text: [character] has been rallying the of [religion] against the spread of [religion], warning that the religion is an existential threat to the state. The priesthood has become increasingly autonomous, acting against the [religion] at every turn and leading persecutions of the religion’s followers. [character] comes to you asking for support against the threat.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Support of the

options.text: Ask for the clergy to help with administrative matters.
Thank them by helping to establish the religion in [city].
Personally thank the clergy for their support.

events.text: The [religion] citizens of [rival] feel content with your rule, happy to be respected and looked after. This good will has spread to the clergy of the religion and the are now some of the most zealous supporters of your rule.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Tales of Leaders Past

options.text: Give your blessing for the poem to be performed.
Decry such false accusations against your ancestors.

requirements.label: Intolerant / Uncouth
tip: The leader must have one of: Intolerant; Uncouth

options.text: Imprison [character] for this slanderous work.

events.text: You are initially surprised to hear that the upset [character] has composed a new work detailing the life of your predecessor [character]. However, although a masterful composition, the majority of the poem explores some rather unsavory parts of the [title]'s personal life which you are uncertain how [character] even discovered. The poet has been performing the piece in [city] and is seeking to spread it around [rival]. The noble houses suggest you take action, worried that this could tarnish the memory of their old leader.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Temple Finances

options.text: Ask [character] to let [character] give his review, but leave it to the priests to make changes.
Instruct the priests to follow whatever changes are instructed.
Push [character] to find ways to siphon more of the funds for the state.

events.text: The temples and shrines of [religion] are important economic centers with hundreds of workers, estates to manage and taxes collected from the people. [character] has been looking into the management of these temples and argues that there is much in their administration that could be improved, a statement that [character] has taken offense at. [character] asks permission to reform the economic organization of the temples. Will you risk the anger of the priests for such changes?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Tempting Faith

options.text: Adopt [religion] as your religion.

tip: As leader: -40 Opinion with all Religions

options.text: Refuse to accept [character] ways.

events.text: , [character] has been persistently seeking audiences to tell you about the <p.is_sub.S2=SUBJECT_ZOROASTRIANISM>sacrificial rituals of<p=SUBJECT_CHRISTIANITY>path to salvation promised by<p=SUBJECT_JUDAISM>sacred texts and prayers of <p=SUBJECT_MANICHAEISM>divine order of beings as dictated by<else>many gods that constitute the pantheon of<end> [religion]. Seeing the purpose and drive that his belief lends [character] makes you question your godless ways. Will the [title] of [rival] turn to faith?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Art of Allegory

options.text: Incorporate the allegorical myths into [religion].
Those tales are a relic of the past.

requirements.label: Poet / Neoplatonist
tip: The leader must have one of: Poet; Neoplatonist

options.text: Argue that the poets were the first philosophers.

events.text: You find [character] and [character] locked in a heated debate over the stories of [religion] and their place in [religion] [rival]. [character] argues for an allegorical interpretation, that they are an attempt by the early poets to provide a moral framework. [character] is unswayed and claims that [character] is trying to cover for the impiety of the early myth makers.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Blood of Heroes

options.text: Accept their claims.
Claim the bloodline as your own.

events.text: The [family] are hosting a festival in their cities to honor. The family are celebrating that their scholars have traced their bloodline back to the legendary hero. Will you refute this claim?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Dangerous Tide

options.text: Lead a persecution of [religion].
Refuse to move against the religion.

events.text: Oracle has had a sign that [religion] is a dangerous threat to [rival], one that must be removed at any cost. The priests are determined that the [religion] population must be persecuted for to be satisfied.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Deified [title]

options.text: Celebrate with festivals across [rival].
Raise a statue in the center of [city] to [character]-.
Fund the cult of [character].

events.text: The of [religion] have declared [character] a god, one of the pantheon. Such an honor will bring glory to your name by association. How will you use the apotheosis of this divine ancestor?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Donatists

options.text: Take no chances and send in the military to stop the conflict.
Ask the Bishops to show moderation with the sect.
Outlaw the rebellious movement.

events.text: The [religion] of [city] are refusing the sacraments of the church after claiming that the city's clergy are sinners, willing to hand over the sacred scriptures and deny their faith when challenged in a recent altercation with the local authorities. The elders of the city have petitioned you for help defusing the conflict between the Donatists and the Orthodoxy.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The End of All Things

options.text: The world must be cleansed and made ready!
These are truly the end times.
I refuse to believe such portents.

events.text: The ideas of Revelation have had a profound effect on [religion]. Anonymous writers have started to spread visions of the end days, which they claim to have received as visions from God. These startling tales are a fever-dream collection of divine beings spilling into the world, often including every form of horror. These ideas are leading some of the faithful to believe that the end of the world is close, perhaps even imminent.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Evangelical

options.text: Embrace the teachings of Jesus.
Politely decline to listen to future sermons.

requirements.label: Intolerant / Impious / Cruel
tip: The leader must have one of: Intolerant; Impious; Cruel

options.text: Send [character] to the dungeons.

events.text: The [religion] are an especially evangelical group, seeing the spreading of the word of God as a core part of their religion. Within the court [character] has led the charge, making regular speeches in front of the gathered nobles to tell the story of the one they call Jesus. The fervor, and length, of the sermons is starting to frustrate the other members of court, who argue that the time taken for such speeches could be used to deal with administrative matters. However, there is something enticing about this promise of eternal forgiveness from the [religion] god.
